title: Properness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$ with $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ along $S_i\to S_0$ and $f:X\to Y$ its base change along $S\to S_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then there is $i\ge0$ such that $f_i$ is proper.

source.place: Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265) in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739), and its proof (Limits Lemmas 01ZQ descend-separated-finite-presentation, 0202 chow-finite-type, 01ZP descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; Schemes Lemma 03GI quasi-compact-permanence; Morphisms Lemmas 01W3 composition-proper, 01W4 base-change-proper, 01W6 image-proper-scheme-closed, 03GN image-proper-is-proper; tags checked in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags)

proof.text: *Step 1 (separated at a finite stage; re-basing).* By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-separated] (Stacks 01ZQ), applicable since $f$ is proper, hence separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], there is $i_1\ge0$ with $f_{i_1}$ separated. The situation at $i_1$ is again one of the kind of the statement: the transition morphism $S_{i_1}\to S_0$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3), and so are its base changes $X_{i_1}\to X_0$, $Y_{i_1}\to Y_0$ (ibid. (1)); as $S_0,X_0,Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so are $S_{i_1},X_{i_1},Y_{i_1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). For $i\ge i_1$ the transition $S_i\to S_0$ is the composite $S_i\to S_{i_1}\to S_0$, so by the transitivity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] ($X_0\times_{S_0}S_i\cong(X_0\times_{S_0}S_{i_1})\times_{S_{i_1}}S_i$, likewise for $Y$ and for $S$ in place of $S_i$) $f_i$ and $f$ are the base changes of $f_{i_1}$ to $S_i$ and to $S$; $f_{i_1}$ is locally of finite type, as a base change of $f_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. An index $i\ge i_1$ is an index $i\ge0$. Replacing $0$ by $i_1$ we may and do assume that $f_0$ is separated (and keep: $S_0,X_0,Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $f_0$ locally of finite type, $f$ proper).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265): 'By Lemma 01ZQ we see that $f_i$ is separated for some $i\ge0$. Replacing $0$ by $i$ we may assume that $f_0$ is separated.' (the re-basing, which the source leaves implicit, written out)

proof.text: *Step 2 (Chow's lemma at the stage $0$).* $f_0$ is quasi-compact, since $X_0$ is quasi-compact and $Y_0$ quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) (Stacks 03GI); so $f_0$ is separated and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]) over the quasi-compact quasi-separated $Y_0$. By Chow's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-chow-finite-type] (Stacks 0202, applied over the base $Y_0$) there are $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'_0$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi_0:X'_0\to X_0$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and an immersion $j_0:X'_0\to P_0:=\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with $p_0\circ j_0=f_0\circ\pi_0$, where $p_0:P_0\to Y_0$ is the projection; $p_0$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper].

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265): 'Observe that $f_0$ is quasi-compact, see Schemes, Lemma 03GI. By Lemma 0202 we can choose a diagram ... where $X_0'\to\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}$ is an immersion, and $\pi:X_0'\to X_0$ is proper and surjective.'

proof.text: *Step 3 (the base changed diagram).* For $T=S_i$ ($i\ge0$) or $T=S$, with $Y_T=Y_0\times_{S_0}T$ ($=Y_i$ resp. $Y$) and $X_T=X_0\times_{S_0}T$, put $X'_T=X'_0\times_{Y_0}Y_T$ and $P_T=P_0\times_{Y_0}Y_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By the definition $\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}=Y_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and the transitivity of fibre products, $P_T\cong\mathbf P^n_{Y_T}$ over $Y_T$, with projection $p_T$ the base change of $p_0$; and $X'_T\cong X'_0\times_{S_0}T$, $P_T\cong P_0\times_{S_0}T$, $X'_T\cong X'_0\times_{P_0}P_T$, $X'_T\cong X'_0\times_{X_0}X_T$ (each by pasting of cartesian squares, using $Y_T=Y_0\times_{S_0}T$ and $X_T=X_0\times_{Y_0}Y_T$). Let $j_T:X'_T\to P_T$ and $\pi_T:X'_T\to X_T$ be the base changes of $j_0$ and $\pi_0$; then $p_T\circ j_T=f_T\circ\pi_T$ ($f_T=f_i$ resp. $f$), being the base change of $p_0\circ j_0=f_0\circ\pi_0$ along $Y_T\to Y_0$. Thus $j_T$ is the base change of the morphism $j_0$ of $S_0$-schemes to $T$, so the pair $(X'_0\to P_0,\ S_0)$ with the system $(S_i)$ is again in the situation of the statement, with $j_i$, $j:=j_S$ as the base changes. Moreover: $j_T$ is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (1); $\pi_T$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b) and surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265): 'Introduce $X'=X_0'\times_{Y_0}Y$ and $X_i'=X_0'\times_{Y_0}Y_i$.' (the identifications of the base changes, left implicit in the source, written out)

proof.text: *Step 4 ($X'\to\mathbf P^n_Y$ is a closed immersion).* Write $X'=X'_S$, $P=P_S=\mathbf P^n_Y$, $p=p_S$, $\pi=\pi_S$. The composite $f\circ\pi:X'\to Y$ is proper, as $\pi$ (step 3) and $f$ are proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a) (Stacks 01W3, 01W4). The projection $p:P\to Y$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], in particular separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $p\circ j=f\circ\pi$ (step 3), so $j$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] (Stacks 01W6). As $j$ is moreover an immersion (step 3), it is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed].

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265): 'By Morphisms, Lemmas 01W3 and 01W4 we see that $X'\to Y$ is proper. Hence $X'\to\mathbf P^n_Y$ is a closed immersion (Morphisms, Lemma 01W6).'

proof.text: *Step 5 (the immersion is closed at a finite stage).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01ZP) to the morphism $j_0:X'_0\to P_0$ of $S_0$-schemes and the system $(S_i)$ (step 3). Its hypotheses: $S_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $X'_0$ is, since $\pi_0$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated (so quasi-separated) [def-weil-proper-morphism], over the quasi-compact quasi-separated $X_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2); $P_0$ is, since $p_0$ is proper over the quasi-compact quasi-separated $Y_0$ (same reasons); $j_0$ is locally of finite type, being an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (2); and its base change $j$ to $S$ is a closed immersion (step 4). Hence there is $i\ge0$ such that $j_i:X'_i\to\mathbf P^n_{Y_i}$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 081F (lemma-eventually-proper, line 3265): 'By Lemma 01ZP we find that $X'_i\to\mathbf P^n_{Y_i}$ is a closed immersion for $i$ large enough.' (the check of the hypotheses of 01ZP, left implicit, written out)

proof.text: *Step 6 ($f_i$ is proper).* For this $i$: $j_i$ is a closed immersion, hence proper, and $p_i:\mathbf P^n_{Y_i}\to Y_i$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], so $p_i\circ j_i=f_i\circ\pi_i:X'_i\to Y_i$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), (a), in particular universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The morphism $\pi_i:X'_i\to X_i$ is surjective (step 3). The morphism $f_i$ is separated and of finite type, as the base change of the separated morphism of finite type $f_0$ (step 2) along $Y_i\to Y_0$ [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] (Stacks 03GN), applied over the base $Y_i$ to $\pi_i$ with $p=f_i\circ\pi_i$ and $q=f_i$, the morphism $f_i$ is universally closed, and being separated and locally of finite type it is proper.

lean.statement: theorem exists_isProper_baseChange_of_isLimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (t : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map t)] (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I) [CompactSpace (D.obj (op i₀))] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj (op i₀))] {X₀ Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀] [CompactSpace Y₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀] (a : X₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) (b : Y₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (h : f₀ ≫ b = a) [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀] (hf : IsProper (pullback.map a (c.π.app (op i₀)) b (c.π.app (op i₀)) f₀ (𝟙 c.pt) (𝟙 (D.obj (op i₀))) ((Category.comp_id a).trans h.symm) ((Category.comp_id _).trans (Category.id_comp _).symm))) : ∃ (i : I) (hi : i₀ ≤ i), IsProper (pullback.map a (D.map (homOfLE hi).op) b (D.map (homOfLE hi).op) f₀ (𝟙 (D.obj (op i))) (𝟙 (D.obj (op i₀))) ((Category.comp_id a).trans h.symm) ((Category.comp_id _).trans (Category.id_comp _).symm))
